title: Quantile-driven batch scaler: continuous profiling and conservative safe-apply
creator: Ava Kapoor
description: Build a quantile-driven batch scaling service that continuously profiles per-workload latency and token distribution, recommends batch size and coalescing window parameters, and performs conservative safe-apply rollouts. Unlike previous heuristics that rely on mean or fixed thresholds, this engine uses tail-aware quantiles (P50/P95/P99) and robust estimators to choose batching parameters that maximize cost reduction while keeping tail latency within SLO headroom.
scope: Service covers: workload fingerprinting (session + request shape), quantile telemetry pipeline, parameter recommendation model (rules + lightweight optimizer), staged safe-apply controller (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> full), rollback heuristics, dashboards and alerts. Integration points: runtime batching layer, KV cache interactions, Console rollout API, and token-level cost breakdown telemetry.
success_metrics: Net hosted cost per 1M tokens decreased by >= 8% for covered workloads
P95 latency regressions <= 3% relative to baseline during steady state
Safe-apply failure rate (rollback required) < 2% of applies
Recommendations adopted automatically (no manual override) for >= 60% of eligible workloads after validation window
acceptance_criteria: Profiler gathers stable quantile estimates for 48h across traffic patterns (burst and steady)
Recommendation engine exposes suggested config JSON and confidence score per workload
Safe-apply controller enforces staged rollout with automatic rollback triggers based on P95, error rate, and cost delta
End-to-end integration tests (shadow and canary) pass in staging with synthetic traffic and fuzzed KV cache hits
Console shows per-workload recommendation, expected cost delta, and A/B comparison dashboard
implementation_notes: Telemetry: augment existing request events with token_count, sequence_length, kv_cache_hit bool, and submission_bucket tag to measure coalescing eligibility
Quantiles: use t-digest for streaming quantile estimation to reduce memory for high-cardinality workloads

Recommendation logic: two-stage approach: (1) rule-based safe candidates (max_batch <= 8 or computed cap from seq_len) then (2) local Bayesian optimizer to explore small adjustments around candidate config
Conservative defaults: start recommends with smaller batch and longer coalesce-window only when P95 headroom >= +20% and KV cache hit rate >= 15%
Conflict resolution: if workload is pinned by customer (pin_version set) skip auto-apply and surface in Console
KV cache: prefer parameterizations that do not evict frequently-used KV entries; include a KV-penalty cost in objective function
Compute cost estimate: translate token/savings into expected GPU-ms saved using profiling tables generated by infra team
rollout_plan: Shadow run: apply recommended batching parameters in shadow mode for 24–72h to collect P50/P95/P99 and cost-proxy metrics without affecting user traffic
Canary apply: target 1–3% of traffic (low-risk customers) for 6h with tight monitoring; if no regression -> ramp to 10%
Staged ramp: double canary footprint every 6h to 50% with automated checks between increments
Full apply: after 72h of stable metrics at >=50% traffic, mark config as recommended and schedule auto-apply for remaining traffic within maintenance window
Rollback policy: immediate rollback if P95 increases > 10% absolute or error-rate increase > 0.5% or cost increases (unexpected) > 5% over baseline in monitoring window
Manual override: Console exposes one-click rollback and allows setting temporary hold for specific customers
monitoring: Per-workload time-series: P50/P95/P99 latency, request rate, token/s, KV cache hit rate
Cost proxy: estimated GPU-ms and estimated $/1k tokens pre/post recommendation
Alert runbook: high-severity alerts for rollback triggers, and low-severity alerts for gradual regressions
Dashboard: A/B comparison pane showing shadow vs baseline quantiles and cost delta with confidence intervals
SLO guardrails: integrate with existing SLO service to suppress applies for workloads currently within 5% of SLO margin
test_plan: Unit tests for quantile estimator and recommendation scoring using synthetic distributions
Integration tests: shadow and canary flows with simulated KV cache hit/miss patterns
Chaos tests: inject latency spikes and backend errors to validate rollback
Performance test: ensure recommendation calc runs < 200ms per workload snapshot and scaler controller can schedule 1000 safe-applies/hour
Staging validation: run on sample production trace replay for 72h and compare recommended config to hand-tuned golden set
